anchor: more gravelled him than aught that had previously occurred
note: Gravelled: puzzled and stuck, as if stopped by gravel.

anchor: a warm night for the latitude
note: Latitude: the distance north or south of the equator.

anchor: dozing on the uppermost deck
note: Dozing: sleeping lightly, half awake, outdoors in the warm night.

anchor: one of hundreds suspended so closely wedged together
note: Hundreds of hammocks hung side by side below decks.

anchor: under the lee of the booms
note: Lee: the sheltered side, away from the wind. Booms are the spare spars stowed on deck.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Booms”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: a piled ridge of spare spars amidships
note: Spars are poles that hold sails. Amidships: in the middle of the ship.

anchor: the launch
note: The launch is the largest boat a warship carries.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Launch”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: deckstation of the forecastlemen
note: Forecastlemen: older sailors stationed forward on the forecastle.

anchor: Slip into the lee forechains
note: The chains are platforms on the ship’s side where the shrouds are fastened, used for sounding.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Chains”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: there is something in the wind
note: A saying for something secret going on.

anchor: a reluctance, almost an incapacity of plumply saying no
note: Plumply: bluntly. Billy finds it hard to say no outright.

anchor: the phlegm tacitly to negative any proposition
note: Phlegm: calm temperament. Tacitly: without words. Negative: to reject.

anchor: a narrow platform, one of six, outside of the high bulwarks
note: Bulwarks: the solid sides of a ship above the deck.

anchor: great dead-eyes and multiple columned lanyards of the shrouds and back-stays
note: Dead-eyes and lanyards tighten the shrouds and backstays, ropes that hold up the masts.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Dead-eyes”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: a non-conformist old tar of a serious turn
note: Non-conformist: a Protestant outside the Church of England. Tar: sailor.

anchor: made it even in daytime his private oratory
note: Oratory: a small place for prayer.

anchor: one of the afterguard
note: The afterguard were the less skilled men stationed near the stern.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “After-guard”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: Hist! Billy
note: Hist: a call for silence.

anchor: held up two small objects faintly twinkling
note: Two coins, as a bribe to join a mutiny.

anchor: the mysterious emissary decamped
note: Emissary: someone sent on a secret errand. Decamped: left quickly.

anchor: an irascible old fellow
note: Irascible: quick to anger, easily annoyed and hot-tempered.

anchor: Red Pepper
note: A nickname for his red face and hot temper.

anchor: to marry to the gunner’s daughter
note: The gunner’s daughter was a sailors’ joke for the gun to which boys were tied to be flogged.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Gunner’s daughter”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: disciplinary castigation
note: Castigation: severe punishment, here a flogging at the gun.

anchor: bigoted in their sea-prejudices
note: Bigoted: stubbornly attached to one’s own opinions.

anchor: territorial encroachments
note: Encroachments: intrusions on someone else’s ground.

anchor: to handle a marlinspike
note: A marlinspike is a pointed iron tool for splicing rope.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Marline-spike”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000
